doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His wife and age
summary: He praises his wife's support and admits musicians are hard to live with.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I want to see you… Ninety years young. [laughs] No. But I’d like to say that, you know, my wife is fantastic.
And I’m not a bargain to live with. No musician is. No. I had…
I’m absentminded. Not absentminded. I only got music in there, you know. And sometimes it’s me, me, me, me, you know. And… she deserve more than a medal. [laughs] Okay, let’s, just…
Well, I wanted to talk about…
[Don’t?] put that in there, you know.
Yeah. I’m glad you did. You have to because, you know, musicians, without a really supportive partner, it’s a difficult life. Or impossible.

Aw, we [inaudible] here. I didn’t do the decoration. I only… I only brought in some… a few dollars to it. This, you know, I know where they come from, but you know, it’s… and in Belgium, the same. They clean our house in Belgium. Anyway, okay.
